<thought>We need to determine how many methyl (CH₃) groups are present in the unknown compound. The most direct way is to retrieve its 13C NMR spectrum, where each distinct carbon environment appears as a signal. Methyl carbons typically resonate in the upfield region (≈10–30 ppm). By counting the number of signals in that region we can infer the number of CH₃ groups. We'll request the 13C NMR data for the sample.</thought>
